source.title: 诊断学（第10版）
source.section: 第五篇 辅助检查 第一章 心电图 第六节

scope: Teaching examples of 3:2, 4:3 and 5:4 Wenckebach cycles, not a clinical AV-node electrophysiological model.
rule: P waves are equally spaced. Conducted beats have progressively increasing PR with authored increments of 80/40/20 ms. The final P in each group is blocked, then the sequence resets. Mechanical events retain their delay relative to electrical events.
constraints: Only the listed 3:2, 4:3 and 5:4 sequences are supported, retaining grouped constraints. The final mechanical offset plus the sequence's largest extra delay must be strictly less than the atrial period. QT uses the atrial period as a conservative lower interval bound, without beatwise adaptation.
verification: Checks exact event times/window boundaries, checkpoints, twelve-lead recovery, delayed pressure/runoff, atomic event budgets, cancellation and times near long.MaxValue, plus native data/pixels in both demos.
unimplemented: Other Wenckebach ratios and variable sequences remain unimplemented.
First escape, capture, fusion and other AV-block examples remain unimplemented.
